frontmatter.title: Resources for a recorded optimization trajectory
frontmatter.description: Complete circuit-batch mapping and conditional physical costs for replaying the original sampled QAOA and VQE records.

children.value: omits sampled training. This report instead maps every measured group in the original four-vertex-cycle QAOA and first two-qubit VQE records, including rejected proposals, incumbent remeasurements, initial calls, and fresh final validation. It treats the stored angles and shot allocations as fixed inputs to a

Replay means preparing the recorded circuits with their recorded repetitions. Fresh hardware measurements are not allowed to choose different parameters in this cost calculation. A hardware-driven optimizer could follow a different angle path, with different synthesis costs and achieved quality, even when its call and shot schedule is fixed.

The circuit mapping and conditional estimator results have separate status in the generated summary below. A checked mapping is not an executed fault-tolerant run. Physical results use an expected synthesis-cost model; they certify neither concrete synthesized sequences nor worst-case work, runtime tails, convergence, or output-error confidence.
The original experiment contains three predetermined seed/start pairs for each task. Its 32-sweep sampled schedule and holdout are documented in the
. Here the workload is the complete collection of those recorded runs, with a separate resource budget for each task.

A VQE objective call contains two groups, all-Z and all-X. QAOA contains one all-Z group. Batch repetition weights retain the exact per-call shot allocation rather than multiplying one final circuit by an optimizer iteration count. The ideal protocol repeats input-state preparation and all basis changes for each shot. Samples in the source experiment were drawn classically from statevector probabilities; these totals are not measured QPU consumption.
conditional resource-model replay of the recorded ideal finite-shot trajectory

. It costs all training, rejected proposals, incumbent remeasurements, and independent validation. It does not predict that a synthesized or noisy hardware optimizer would follow the same path or return the same outcomes.

The validated ledger contains 780 calls, 1,074 measured-group batches and 1,052,928 modeled preparations. Every batch has a full small-circuit Operator check up to global phase and an unchanged final measurement map. Only then are 127 exact source QASM and 127 exact lowered QASM artifacts deduplicated.

Resource-query reuse is separate from exact-QASM deduplication. Cost-canonical raw and transformed PSSPC Trace JSON must match exactly in ordered instructions, repetitions, qubits, base error, resource states and all cost properties under the same profile and budgets. Only the documented QDK
CPU-import instrumentation is omitted from the cost key; its complete original JSON is retained. Different-angle unitaries are not declared equal.

The distinct-QASM physical-cost probe retains every fingerprint field. Only positive finite factory error-rate floats may agree within four adjacent binary64 values; all other values, types and structures remain exact. Both full fingerprints and every differing float path, raw value and ULP distance are preserved. This narrowly bounded numeric agreement is not a synthesis or accuracy certificate.
There are 8 verified cost signatures and 9 bounded real QDK queries, including a second distinct-QASM probe of one shared cost signature. The task physical-fault allowance is
uniformly across all preparations: QAOA has 473,856 and VQE 579,072 preparations. Each execution separately receives synthesis-model scalar allowance
; that coherent model scalar is not summed over shots as a stochastic fault probability.

, 100 ns gates and 500 ns measurements. Times sum per-preparation model runtimes; peaks take the maximum across independently selected signature layouts/factories. Configuration changes, transport, resets and adaptive feedback are unmeasured, and no common physical configuration or joint Pareto frontier is certified.

The recorded CPU controller/evaluator times are supplied separately in the manifest; they are not added to quantum-model runtime. The PSSPC rotation costs are a mean-fit projection, not concrete certified synthesis sequences, worst-case bounds, runtime-tail guarantees, or observable/optimizer accuracy guarantees. Statistical uncertainty, coherent synthesis-model allowance and stochastic physical-fault allocations remain distinct.
From every sampled batch to an explicit circuit

children.label: From every sampled batch to an explicit circuit

children.value: binds the replay to the source run record, generator, environment, and implementation. The
identifies the task, run, seed, training or validation phase, call, measurement group, parameters, and shot repetitions for every batch.

Each batch has source and lowered measured OpenQASM files identified by SHA-256. QAOA includes H preparation, edge phases, and mixer rotations. VQE includes its RY/CX preparation and the all-X H basis changes where required. Final qubit-to-classical measurement maps are retained. Initial all-zero availability is an assumption; physical reset time is excluded where unmeasured.

For every batch, the small-system check compares source and lowered unitary operators up to a global phase before final measurement, and verifies the final measurement map separately. That check validates numerical lowering of each particular circuit. It does not validate an approximate Clifford+T replacement of its arbitrary angles.

Identical QASM content can share a stored file by its exact hash. Every original batch still has an execution-mapping entry and its own repetition weight. Exact file deduplication therefore reduces artifact duplication without removing objective evaluations or shots.
Share estimator work only when the native cost model agrees

children.label: Share estimator work only when the native cost model agrees

children.value: Different fitted angles generally produce different unitaries. Resource-model grouping makes no claim that those unitaries are equivalent. Equal gate counts alone also do not establish equal cost: native trace ordering, repetitions, properties, and resource requirements can affect the estimator.
groups batches after comparing cost-canonical native and PSSPC trace JSON, with the recorded derived metadata. Complete instrumented trace JSON is retained. The cost signature excludes only native

instrumentation, property 7, whose recorded pinned-source audit establishes that it is not consumed by the physical cost calculation. All other fields and properties remain in the comparison. This CPU instrumentation time is not quantum runtime.
The grouping uses the same synthesis setting, physical profile, and per-execution budget. Its equality is equality of inputs relevant to this pinned

, rather than equality of circuit behavior at different angles. A bounded second-QASM probe for a shared model class is recorded separately, comparing actual physical Pareto fields under the same budget and profile. Its scope and result are retained rather than treated as a general circuit-equivalence proof.

QDK’s default OpenQASM importer constructs a canonical trace from logical counts, already abstracting continuous angles and original Clifford topology. Comparing those native traces checks equality of inputs inside the declared estimator model; it does not certify a routed schedule for every original gate. The source and lowered QASM, gate counts, measurement maps, and numerical lowering checks preserve the original circuit evidence separately.
Each group retains a representative input and maps all constituent batches to the corresponding estimator report. Their repetition weights are summed only after the model-signature comparison. The
retain the actual estimator outputs and model provenance. The distinction between source-circuit equivalence checks and cost-model grouping is essential: neither substitutes for the other.

children.value: The report checks this allocation across all batches. A union-bound interpretation requires the estimator’s per-execution physical contribution to be a calibrated upper bound for the hardware/model assumptions; the replay does not supply that experimental calibration. Independence of physical faults is not needed for the union bound.
Each prepared circuit also receives a

. This is a coherent approximation-model quantity, not a stochastic failure probability. It is not multiplied by the million-shot total and labeled whole-run failure. Each shot prepares a fresh state; repeated preparations do not form one long coherent computation on a shared state. Repetition also does not remove systematic observable bias from an approximate circuit. Adaptive classical feedback can turn changed outcomes into a different parameter path; no approximation or accuracy bound for that complete classical–quantum process is established here.
The pinned Microsoft QDK resource estimator 1.34.0 and native PSSPC model use the audited expected rotation-cost fit

. The fit is not an executed synthesis sequence, an instance-specific approximation certificate, a worst-case cost bound, or a bound on fallback-protocol runtime tails. The
model allowance consequently does not certify the final cut value or energy error. Sampling uncertainty, fitted quality, and physical-fault allocation remain separate quantities.
The two physical profiles retain the frozen

physical error rates, 100 ns gate time, and 500 ns measurement time. The Grover baseline remains unchanged. This report does not alter requested problem quality or hardware assumptions to manufacture an improvement.
Aggregate serial time and peak footprint with explicit exclusions

children.label: Aggregate serial time and peak footprint with explicit exclusions

children.value: For a declared model-point selection, serial quantum time is weighted by every batch’s shot count and peak footprint is the maximum selected footprint:

children.html: Tserial=∑bNb tb,Qpeak=max⁡bqb.T_{\mathrm{serial}}=\sum_b N_b\,t_b,\qquad Q_{\mathrm{peak}}=\max_b q_b.Tserial​=b∑​Nb​tb​,Qpeak​=bmax​qb​.

children.value: The declared choices can select independent per-model-signature Pareto points. Configuration changes, transport, communication, routing, physical reset, and feedback overhead are excluded where unmeasured. A single common physical layout or factory configuration for the complete trajectory is not certified. Thus these aggregate choices are conditional serial model costs, rather than a measured machine schedule or a globally optimized architecture.

The local CPU-control and objective-simulation timings from the original experiment are reported separately. A simulator’s control time is not a measurement of classical feedback latency in a fault-tolerant processor, and it is not silently added to or hidden inside quantum runtime. Concurrent execution, reuse across shots, and latency overlap require separate scheduling evidence.
Reproduction requires the original sampled run record, its matching implementation, and a source checkout containing the shared

adapter in the pinned Python 3.12/QDK environment. The manifest and signature records identify the executed code, declared model settings, and input hashes. Standalone sampled experiment downloads remain available through the
; exporting the shared physical adapter is a separate integration step.
